claims.text: The test alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr, corresponding to 20 at.% of each element.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has a chemically disordered microstructure.
The multi-principal-element composition of WTaTiVZr produces significant local lattice distortion.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has a refined, possibly nanocrystalline, grain structure and consequently a high density of grain boundaries.
Lattice distortion and grain refinement shift deformation in WTaTiVZr from dislocation-mediated slip toward grain-boundary sliding and intergranular plastic flow.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation reduces localized stress concentrations in the alloy.
The proposed microstructure promotes defect recombination.
Grain-boundary sliding, stress redistribution, and defect recombination delay crack initiation and propagation.
At temperatures of at least 800°C, WTaTiVZr will have greater uniform plastic strain and toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
The WTaTiVZr alloy will show more ductile stress-strain behavior and delayed cracking relative to pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten deforms primarily by dislocation-mediated slip and, under the stated conditions, tends toward dislocation exhaustion, pile-ups, crack propagation, and brittle failure.
Pure tungsten has a more limited capacity for grain-boundary-mediated plasticity than the proposed WTaTiVZr microstructure.
The proposed enhancement applies primarily above approximately 800°C.
Significant grain coarsening would diminish the proposed mechanical benefit.
Departures from equimolar WTaTiVZr chemistry could diminish the proposed mechanical benefit.
A comparison using WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten specimens with comparable grain sizes, strain rates, and thermal histories can test the role of chemical complexity while limiting grain-size effects.
Stress-strain measurements, in-situ microscopy, and post-mortem fractography can distinguish enhanced strain and toughness and assess grain-boundary sliding, dislocation activity, and crack paths.
Failure to observe both a statistically significant increase in plastic strain and toughness and predominant grain-boundary-mediated plasticity would falsify the proposed primary mechanism.
